subtitle: דלאלהֵ אלחאירין — The Guide of the Perplexed
author: Moses Maimonides (1138–1204)
intro: Kisse first means 'chair' — and because only the great are seated on a chair, it came to signify greatness itself. So the Sanctuary and heaven are each called God's 'throne' insofar as they indicate the greatness of the One manifested in them. Where Scripture speaks of God's throne it means His majesty, never a body He sits upon; to imagine Him existent-without-throne and existent-with-throne, Maimonides warns, is outright unbelief. Hover a phrase to see its English light up; tap any word for a gloss; dotted words are key terms.

terms.note: Primary sense: a chair, the seat of kings; hence a symbol of greatness. Of God it denotes His majesty — never a literal seat — whether predicated of the Sanctuary, of heaven, or of Him directly.
Called a 'throne of glory' because it indicates the greatness of the One who was manifested in it and let His light and dignity alight upon it.

terms.gloss: to be manifested (of the divine light)
terms.note: The Sanctuary and heaven are 'thrones' because the divine light was manifested (tajallā) upon them — a manifestation of glory, not a localization of God's body.
Maimonides' recurring formula for semantic extension: 'the language broadened' a term beyond its primary sense — here, kisse from a literal chair to a figure of majesty.

aligned.ja: ולמא כאן אלכרסי אנמא יג'לס עליה אהל אלג'לאלה ואלעט'מה כאלמלוך, וצאר אלכרסי שיא מא מוג'ודא ידל עלי עט'מהֵ מן אהל לה וג'לאלתה ועט'ם שאנה, סמי אלמקדש כסא לדלאלתה עלי עט'מהֵ מן תג'לי פיה ואחל נורה ווקארה עליה, פקאל כסא כבוד מרום מראשון וכו'.
aligned.en: And since the chair is that on which only people of majesty and greatness, such as kings, are seated, and the chair became some existing thing that indicates the greatness of one worthy of it, his majesty and the grandeur of his estate, the Sanctuary was called 'throne' for its indicating the greatness of the One who was manifested in it and let His light and dignity alight upon it; so it said, 'a throne of glory, on high from the beginning' (Jer 17:12), and so forth.

aligned.ja: ומן אג'ל הד'א אלמעני סמית אלסמא כסא, לדלאלתהא ענד מן יערפהא ויעתברהא עלי עט'מהֵ מוג'דהא ומחרכהא ומדבר אלעאלם אלספלי בפיץ' ג'ודהא, פקאל כה אמר י״י השמים כסאי וכו'.
aligned.en: And for this meaning heaven was called 'throne,' for its indicating, to one who knows and considers it, the greatness of the One who brought it into being, who moves it and governs the lower world by the overflow of its bounty; so it said, 'thus says the Lord: the heaven is My throne' (Isa 66:1), and so forth.

aligned.ja: הד'א הו אלד'י ינבגי אן יעתקדה אלמחקקון, לא אן ת'ם ג'סם ירתפע אלאלאה עליה, תעאלי עלוא כבירא, אד' סיתברהן לך אנה תעאלי גיר ג'סם. פכיף יכון לה מכאן או מקר עלי ג'סם?
aligned.en: This is what the verifiers ought to believe — not that there is some body upon which the Deity is raised up, exalted be He greatly; for it will be demonstrated to you that He, may He be exalted, is no body. How then could He have a place or a resting-spot upon a body?

aligned.en: Rather the matter is as we alerted you: every place that God honored and singled out with His light and splendor — such as the Sanctuary or heaven — was called 'throne.'
